subject.title: Track OpenClaw seams needed for full imported-plugin parity

question: Which requested host seams should OpenClaw commit to as public contracts, and in what staged order should Babelfish depend on them?
rationale: The work defines permanent plugin, authorization, connector, and bundle-ownership boundaries; implementation cannot safely choose those contracts without host maintainer intent and security review.

options.title: Stage narrow host contracts
options.body: Approve and specify each seam independently, beginning with existing internal bundle behavior that can be exposed without duplicating ownership.

options.title: Design one parity API program
options.body: Treat all requested seams as one coordinated SDK initiative, accepting a larger design and review cycle before Babelfish integration.

options.title: Keep mappings unsupported
options.body: Decline new public contracts for now and continue exposing these imported contributions as unsupported rather than approximating them.

recommendation.title: Stage narrow host contracts
recommendation.body: Approve and specify each seam independently, beginning with existing internal bundle behavior that can be exposed without duplicating ownership.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the cross-ecosystem gap analysis and are the only evidence-backed repository member connected to the requested direction in the supplied context.
